research.website_note: The results repeatedly identify duolingo.com as Duolingo’s own official site and investor/handbook/blog pages belong to Duolingo, Inc.

strategy.observation: Duolingo says it runs 1,000+ A/B tests per quarter and that most growth investment is concentrated in product R&D, indicating an engineering organization centered on rapid software experimentation.
strategy.offer_link: Bulk supply of school uniforms has no direct connection to that experimentation-heavy product engineering focus; it would only be relevant if Duolingo were separately procuring uniforms for a disclosed school or field program, which is not supported by the facts.
hypotheses: Duolingo may have some unrelated education or community initiative that requires apparel procurement, but that is not confirmed.
The recipient may oversee non-product operations or vendor purchasing in addition to engineering, but that is an assumption.
strategy.angle: With 1,000+ A/B tests a quarter and growth spend aimed at product R&D, your engineering team is clearly built around software experimentation, not apparel procurement.
strategy.fit_reason: A bulk school-uniform offer does not plausibly map to Duolingo’s product-led, software-heavy engineering priorities, and none of the facts suggest a school, campus, or apparel-buying use case for the VP of Engineering.

draft.subject: School uniform sourcing
draft.body:
Noticed Duolingo runs 1,000+ A/B tests each quarter, and most growth spend seems to sit in product R&D. That reads like a team built for rapid software iteration, not vendor wrangling.

I supply bulk school uniforms for organizations that need a straightforward source for school or field programs. If Duolingo has any separate education initiative that ever needs that kind of procurement, who handles it on your side?
